Concept Definition: The Paris Agreement goals refer to the international commitments made by countries to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius, and to enhance the ability to adapt to climate change impacts.

Resource Description: The 2024 edition of the IEA’s World Energy Outlook discusses the challenges of energy access, with 750 million people lacking electricity and over 2 billion without clean cooking fuels, predominantly in sub-Saharan Africa. The report also addresses the current trajectory of global energy transitions, warning of a potential rise of 2.4°C in global temperatures by 2100 if current policies persist.

Concept Definition: Sustainable energy refers to energy sources that are environmentally friendly and can be maintained over the long term without depleting resources or harming the ecosystem. Renewable energy is a subset of sustainable energy that comes from natural processes that are continuously replenished, such as solar, wind, and hydro power.
Resource Title: Global Energy Perspective 2024
Resource Description: IRENA’s World Energy Transition Outlook highlights that the global energy transition is falling short, jeopardizing the achievement of the 1.5°C climate goal set at COP21 nearly a decade ago. While there is still time to act, an urgent course correction is essential to realign with this target. Achieving this requires addressing the structural and systemic barriers that continue to hinder progress in the energy transition.

Concept Definition: A just energy transition refers to the shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources in a way that is fair and equitable, ensuring that all communities, especially those historically marginalized, benefit from the transition and are not left behind.
Resource Title: World Energy Transitions Outlook 2024
Resource Description: The Global Energy Perspective 2024 provides a comprehensive demand outlook for 68 sectors and 78 fuels, aligned with a 1.5°C pathway under the Paris Agreement. It also introduces three updated bottom-up energy transition scenarios, redesigned to account for evolving global conditions such as geopolitical challenges, complex supply chains, and rising inflation.

Resource Description: The report evidences that transforming the clean cooking landscape is a complex endeavour with no straight-forward solutions, but one that requires the establishment of clear policies and robust regulatory frameworks as foundational elements for attracting and driving investment in clean cooking projects.

Concept Definition: The energy value chain refers to the full range of processes involved in the production, distribution, and consumption of energy, including extraction, generation, transmission, and end-use.

Resource Description: This study aims to examine the complexity of the interconnections between energy and the SDGs, as well as give examples of how these linkages can be quantified.

Concept Definition: The water-energy-food nexus refers to the interconnectedness of water, energy, and food systems, highlighting how the management of one resource affects the others, and emphasizing the need for integrated approaches to ensure sustainability and security in these critical areas.

Resource Description: This report is builds on existing studies and quantifies and compares 30 environmental and socioeconomic impact metrics in two different energy scenarios for the future. It also presents a framework for establishing the nature-positive energy transformation that is essential to achieving critical climate and sustainable development goals.

Resource Description: Energy Efficiency 2024 is the IEA’s primary annual analysis on global energy efficiency developments, showing recent trends in energy intensity and demand, prices and policies. The report provides sector-specific analysis on buildings, appliances, industry and transport and explores system-wide themes such as electrification, flexibility, investment and employment. This report is launched in parallel with the new IEA Energy Efficiency Progress Tracker.

Concept Definition: Waste-to-energy solutions are processes that convert non-recyclable waste materials into usable forms of energy, typically electricity or heat, through methods such as combustion, gasification, or anaerobic digestion.

Resource Description: The study aims to analyze the implementations and benefits of digital technologies across various aspects of the energy industry. It specifically discusses the impact of the digitalization of energy on achieving Sustainable Development Goals, highlighting the benefits and challenges it can bring.

Resource Description: The “Intersectionality resource guide and toolkit”, a UN Women and United Nations Partnership on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities led collaborative initiative with support from United Nations and non-United Nations entities, aims to help both organizations and individual practitioners and experts to address intersectionality in policies and programmes.

Concept Definition: Energy diversification refers to the strategy of using a variety of energy sources and technologies to meet energy needs, reducing dependence on a single source and enhancing energy security.
Resource Title: Gender Mainstreaming: A Global Strategy for Achieving Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women and Girls
Resource Description: This brief sets a strategy for gender mainstreaming at programmatic and institutional levels to achieve transformative gender results.

Concept Definition: Integrated power markets refer to interconnected electricity markets that allow for the seamless exchange of electricity across different regions or countries, promoting competition, efficiency, and reliability in energy supply.
Resource Title: Leaving No One Behind: Equality and Non-Discrimination at the Heart of Sustainable Development
Resource Description: This publication sets out a conceptual framework that includes equality (the imperative of moving towards substantive equality of opportunity and outcomes for all groups), non-discrimination and the broader concept of equity.

Resource Title: Implementing the  Water–Energy–Food–Ecosystems Nexus and Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals
Resource Description: This publication compiles a number of case studies with the aim of highlighting the importance and benefits of the WEFE Nexus approach for development cooperation. It identifies pathways for a more integrated and sustainable use of resources that goes beyond traditional sector-specific development silos.

Concept Definition: Low-carbon transport refers to transportation methods and systems that produce minimal greenhouse gas emissions, often through the use of renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, public transit, cycling, and walking.
Resource Title: Integrating the Three Dimensions of Sustainable Development - A Frameworks & Tools
Resource Description: This publication was produced to assist policymakers in addressing the question of how to achieve integration across the policy cycle and to assess levels of integration. This publication is a first step towards meeting the needs of policymakers for frameworks and tools to integrate the three dimensions of sustainable development.

Concept Definition: Sustainable heating refers to methods of heating spaces that minimize environmental impact, often using renewable energy sources, energy efficiency practices, and low-carbon technologies.
Resource Title: Life Cycle Assessment in Renewable Energy: Solar and Wind Perspectives
Resource Description: The article underscores the significance of material selection in photovoltaic, solar, and wind systems, providing a critical overview of the current state of LCA research in renewable energy and stressing the need for standardized methodologies.

Energy Access - Core Concepts

Module Title: Energy Access and Inclusive Energy Services
Description: This lesson offers a global overview of energy access, highlighting its critical role in human rights, poverty reduction, and inclusive sustainable development.
Concept Definition: Energy access refers to the ability of individuals and communities to obtain reliable and affordable energy services, such as electricity and clean cooking fuels, necessary for their daily activities and economic development.
Resource Title: Renewable Energy and the Right to Development: Realizing Human Rights for Sustainable Development
Resource Description: This publication highlights the critical role of renewable energy in advancing human rights, economic development and climate action. It emphasizes the need for equitable energy access and policy reforms to ensure a just transition while safeguarding vulnerable population and preventing human rights abuses in energy projects.

Concept Definition: The basic requirements for energy that are essential for human survival and well-being, including energy for heating, cooking, lighting, and basic transportation.
Resource Title: Guidelines for developing inclusive energy infrastructure
Resource Description: This publication aims to bridge the gap in inclusive energy infrastructure development, focusing on practical strategies for sustainable energy solutions in developing countries and fragile contexts. These guidelines support stakeholders in creating resilient and equitable energy systems.

Concept Definition: Inclusive energy services refer to energy solutions that are accessible, affordable, and equitable for all individuals and communities, particularly marginalized or underserved populations, ensuring that everyone can benefit from reliable energy access.
Resource Description: Accelerating the Productive Use of Electricity : Enabling Energy Access to Power Rural Economic Growth.

Lesson Title: Sustainable Energy to power development
Description: This lesson focuses on  the critical requirements to ensure sustainable energy access, including the building blocks of sustainable energy access
Concept Definition: Energy and development economics is the study of how energy resources and policies impact economic growth, social development, and environmental sustainability in different regions.
Resource Title: A Vision for Clean Cooking Access for All
Resource Description: This report by the IEA and African Development Bank highlights global clean cooking trends, with a focus on Africa’s urgent needs. It examines the current state, costs of inaction, and benefits of achieving UN SDG 7, providing country-level assessments and a roadmap for universal access through targeted policies, technologies, and investments.

Concept Definition: Sustainable energy access refers to the ability of all individuals and communities to obtain reliable, affordable, and clean energy sources that meet their needs without compromising the environment or future generations.
Resource Title: African Energy Outlook 2022
Resource Description: Part of the IEA's World Energy Outlook series, this report outlines pathways to achieve Africa’s energy goals, including universal energy access by 2030. It addresses infrastructure needs, financing, policy priorities, a shifting fuel mix, and just transition issues like affordability and employment.

Resource Title: World Energy Outlook 2024
Resource Description: The IEA’s World Energy Outlook 2024 provides an analysis on global energy trends, focusing on the implications for energy security, emissions, and economic development amid rising geopolitical tensions. This year’s report highlights the rapid growth of clean energy investment and electricity demand, assessing global progress toward a more sustainable energy system. It also includes scenario-based insights on key uncertainties, such as the impact of AI, heatwaves, and policy shifts on the future of energy.

Lesson Title: Energy Poverty and Fuel Poverty
Description: This lesson covers the reality of energy poverty, its causes and impacts, and the tools to measure the challenge of addressing this issue
Concept Definition: Fuel poverty is a situation where a household cannot afford to keep their home adequately warm due to high energy costs, low income, or poor energy efficiency.
Resource Title: Lost in the dark: A survey of energy poverty from space 2024
Resource Description: This report presents a groundbreaking analysis of global energy poverty using high-resolution nighttime satellite imagery. The authors introduce new metrics through the High-Resolution Electricity Access (HREA) platform, offering a spatially detailed, and consistent method to track electricity use, access, and reliability.

Concept Definition: Energy Poverty is a lack of access to adequate, affordable, reliable, and high-quality energy services that are also environmentally friendly. This lack of access impacts various aspects of life, including lighting, cooking, heating, and overall economic development opportunities.
Resource Title: Energy Poverty: Addressing the Intersection of Sustainable Development Goals, 2021
Resource Description: Published in collaboration with the G20, this report examines the multifaceted nature of energy poverty and its connections to various Sustainable Development Goals. It emphasizes the necessity for integrated policies that simultaneously address energy access, economic development, and environmental sustainability, offering policy recommendations to alleviate energy poverty in developing nations.

Resource Title: State of Access to Modern Energy Cooking Services
Resource Description: Published by the World Bank's Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP), this report focuses on the challenges and progress related to access to modern energy cooking services. It emphasizes that approximately 2.6 billion people globally still lack access to clean cooking solutions, leading to significant health and environmental issues. The report provides data-driven insights and policy recommendations to accelerate access to modern cooking energy services.

Lesson Title: The Energy Access Landscape
Chapter Title: Current Status, Trends and Barriers to Energy Access
Description: This lesson provides an overview of the key characteristics and statistics of the disparities in access to energy services
Concept Definition: Energy access for informal settlements refers to the availability and affordability of reliable energy services, such as electricity and clean cooking fuels, for residents living in unplanned or informal housing areas, ensuring they can meet their basic energy needs and improve their quality of life.
Resource Title: Human Development Report 2023-24. Breaking the gridlock: Reimagining cooperation in a polarized world
Resource Description: This report explores how rising inequality, political polarization, and fragmented global cooperation are creating a dangerous gridlock in addressing urgent global challenges. It calls for a reinvigorated multilateralism to overcome this paralysis and reimagine cooperation in a rapidly changing and interconnected world.

Concept Definition: Energy in crisis settings refers to the provision and management of energy resources in areas affected by emergencies, such as natural disasters, armed conflicts, or humanitarian crises, where access to reliable energy is critical for survival, recovery, and rebuilding efforts.
Resource Title: Small Island Developing States at a Crossroads: Towards equitable energy access in least-electrified countries
Resource Description: This report highlights the urgent need for equitable energy access in the least-electrified SIDS, which also face overlapping challenges like poverty, food insecurity, and climate vulnerability. It advocates for decentralized renewable energy over fossil fuel expansion, presenting case studies from Guinea-Bissau, Papua New Guinea, and Vanuatu to illustrate the potential development benefits.

Concept Definition: The global energy gap refers to the disparity between the world's energy demand and the available energy supply, highlighting the need for increased energy production and sustainable solutions to meet future energy needs.
Resource Title: Leaving No One Behind - Rethinking Energy Access Programs in Displacement Settings
Resource Description: This report, Leaving No One Behind – Rethinking Energy Access Programs in Displacement Settings, explores how access to energy can improve the lives of forcibly displaced persons, who are often among the most vulnerable and overlooked populations. It offers a set of actionable recommendations to reshape energy access interventions in displacement contexts, emphasizing the World Bank and ESMAP’s role in leading inclusive, sustainable, and development-focused solutions.

Lesson Title: Status and Trends
Description: This lesson focuses on current status and trends on the global energy gap including access to fundamental energy needs: electricity, clean cooking, heating and cooling. Each part examines the unique challenges aand progress withtin these critical areas
Concept Definition: Access to clean cooking refers to the availability and use of safe, efficient, and environmentally friendly cooking methods and fuels, which reduce health risks and environmental impact compared to traditional cooking practices.
Resource Title: Access to Electricity - SDG7: Data and Projections, 2024
Resource Description: This report provides data and projections related to global electricity access. It focuses on recent metrics on electricity deficits, presents regional insights, tracks progress and presents future projections in energy access.

Key Concept: heating and cooling fuels and technologies
Concept Definition: Heating and cooling fuels and technologies refer to the various energy sources (like natural gas, electricity, and renewable options) and systems (such as furnaces, heat pumps, and air conditioners) used to regulate indoor temperatures for comfort and efficiency.
Resource Title: Energizing health: accelerating electricity access in health-care facilities, 2023
Resource Description: This report offers a detailed overview of the status of energy access in health-care facilities across low- and middle-income countries, outlining key technical, financial, and policy actions needed to achieve universal electrification. It serves as a resource for governments, investors, and development actors involved in planning, financing, and implementing energy solutions to strengthen health systems.

Resource Title: Achieving Universal Access by 2030 and Net-Zero Emissions by 2050: A Global Roadmap for Just and Inclusive Clean Cooking Transition
Resource Description: This UN-Energy policy brief presents a global roadmap to achieve universal access to clean cooking by 2030 and net-zero emissions in the cooking sector by 2050. It outlines key milestones, investment needs, and policy actions required for a just and inclusive clean cooking transition, emphasizing benefits for health, gender equity, and climate while highlighting the role of governments, development partners, and private sector actors.

Lesson Title: Challenges for universal energy access
Description: This lesson explores the complex challenges obstructing equitable acccess to sustainable energy, highlighting issues in infrastructure and capacity, uneven distirbtuion of investments and the need for comprehensive measurement approaches.
Concept Definition: Energy affordability refers to the ability of individuals or households to pay for the energy they need without compromising their basic living standards or financial stability.
Resource Title: Geopolitics of the Energy Transition. Energy Security, 2024
Resource Description: This report explores how the global shift to renewable energy is reshaping the concept of energy security. It examines emerging trade patterns, regional interdependencies, and infrastructure challenges, urging policymakers to move beyond fossil fuel-era thinking and adopt a multidimensional, resilience-focused approach for the renewable energy era.

Concept Definition: Financial de-risking strategies are methods used by organizations to reduce financial risks associated with investments or projects, often by diversifying funding sources, securing insurance, or implementing risk management practices.
Resource Title: Grid planning under uncertainty: Investing for the energy transition, 2023
Resource Description: This report explores how electric grid planners must adapt to rising climate risks, rapid electrification, and growing demand by adopting more integrated, predictive, and granular planning strategies. It highlights the need for new tools, data, and performance metrics to ensure that grid investments are resilient, efficient, and aligned with the energy transition and customer expectations.

Resource Title: Informal Settlements: No Longer Invisible: The role of impact in scaling capital mobilisation to fund slum-upgrading programmes globally, 2022
Resource Description: This report makes the case for placing urban informality at the center of the global impact investment agenda. It highlights the immense social, economic, and environmental challenges faced by over a billion people living in slums across the Global South, and proposes innovative financial instruments to scale investment in slum upgrading and unlock transformative development opportunities.

Lesson Title: An Intersectional Approach
Chapter Title: Bridging the Energy Access Gap
Description: This lesson explores  how an intersectional approach can transform energy access by addressing the overlapping identities that shape people's experience and challenges. The lesson presents practical strategies to operationalize intersectionality in sustainable energy acces sprogramming.
Concept Definition: Inclusive and sustainable energy access refers to the ability of all individuals and communities, regardless of their socio-economic status, to obtain reliable, affordable, and clean energy services that support their needs while promoting environmental sustainability.
Resource Title:
HOW CAN ENERGY ACCESS PROGRAMMES ADDRESS
THE NEEDS OF PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES? 2021
Resource Description: Over one billion people globally need assistive products to lead healthy, productive lives, yet 90% lack access. This checklist, developed by Efficiency for Access, aims to support energy access programs and off-grid appliance manufacturers in designing solutions that meet the needs of people with disabilities.

Resource Title: Inclusive energy access in emergencies, a handbook for humanitarians, 2020
Resource Description: This handbook equips humanitarian practitioners with practical tools to improve inclusive energy access in emergencies. It provides a roadmap to address the energy-related needs, safety considerations, and empowerment opportunities that make an immense difference in the lives of women, girls, and other commonly marginalized groups.

Resource Title: Intersectionality resource guide and toolkit. An Intersectional Approach to Leave No One Behind
Resource Description: This Resource Guide and Toolkit provides a practical framework to apply intersectionality, bridging theory and practice. It helps practitioners address intersecting inequalities, embedding an intersectional mindset to advance the 2030 Agenda and its goals.

Lesson Title: Technological Solutions
Description: The lesson highlights the key technological solutions that can accelerate the path towards universal energy access while supporting the transition to clean energy.
Concept Definition: E-cooking refers to the use of electric appliances and devices for cooking food, which can include methods such as induction cooking, electric ovens, and microwaves, often emphasizing energy efficiency and sustainability.
Resource Title: No time to waste: Pathways to deliver clean cooking for all, 2025
Resource Description: This policy brief outlines UNDP's commitment to addressing inequities in clean cooking access, emphasizing its role in integrating energy, climate, and sustainable development efforts to improve lives. It provides policy recommendations to scale up clean cooking solutions, advance equity and social justice, and foster partnerships to enhance financing and programming for clean cooking in developing countries.

Concept Definition: Mini-grids are small-scale power generation and distribution systems that can operate independently or in conjunction with the main electrical grid, providing electricity to local communities, often in remote or underserved areas.
Resource Title: Off-Grid Solar Market Trends Report 2024. ESMAP, 2024
Resource Description: Comprehensive analysis of off-grid solar market trends (2022–2023), highlighting resilience amid global challenges and investment needs for universal energy access by 2030. Published by ESMAP and WB, this go-to resource informs investors, policymakers, and industry stakeholders on solar market dynamics.

Concept Definition: Off-grid renewable energy systems are energy setups that generate power independently from the traditional electricity grid, using renewable sources like solar, wind, or hydro, to provide energy for homes or communities.
Resource Title: Powering progress: market creation strategies for solar e-cooking technologies in off-grid and displaced communities, 2024
Resource Description: Explores off-grid solar e-cooking as a dual solution for climate change mitigation and adaptation. This WFP report emphasizes the role of clean cooking in reducing CO2 emissions and advancing economic development, health, gender equality, and environmental sustainability in low-income settings.

Lesson Title: Financing Mechanisms
Description: This lesson explains how financing mechanisms can incentivize energy access and inclusive energy services with a focus on underserved and vulnerable communities.
Concept Definition: Microfinancing is a financial service that provides small loans and financial support to individuals or small businesses, typically in developing countries, to help them start or expand their operations.
Resource Title: Derisking Renewable Energy Investment: Off-Grid Electrification, 2018
Resource Description: This report provides a framework to help policymakers in developing countries attract private investment in solar PV-battery mini-grids. It outlines public policy and financial instruments to reduce, transfer, or compensate for investment risks in off-grid energy markets, using case studies in Kenya and Uttar Pradesh, India to demonstrate how targeted derisking strategies can lower financing costs, improve affordability, and catalyze private sector investment to accelerate universal electricity access.

Concept Definition: Pay as you go models are payment systems where customers pay for services or products in advance or as they use them, rather than committing to long-term contracts or upfront costs.
Resource Title: Public finance for universal energy access, 2024
Resource Description: This IRENA brief provides a practical tool for policymakers and public financiers to monitor and enhance the effectiveness of public funding for energy access. It aims to map financing needs across the energy access ecosystem, highlight barriers to scaling public investment, and reflect stakeholder preferences for financial instruments, intermediaries, and target beneficiaries.

Concept Definition: Result-based financing models are financial mechanisms that provide funding based on the achievement of specific outcomes or results, rather than on the inputs or processes used to achieve them.
Resource Title: Clean Cooking: Financing Appliances For End Users, 2021
Resource Description: This report explores how end-user financing can accelerate access to clean cooking technologies in low-income markets. It reviews pricing, affordability challenges, and a wide range of emerging financing models while calling for donor support to scale these solutions and make clean cooking affordable for the poorest households.

Lesson Title: Policy Frameworks
Description: This lesson explores three policy instruments: subsidies, tax incentives and regulatory reforms, and how they contribute to the promotion of sustainable energy solutions.
Concept Definition: Financial support from the government to promote energy production or consumption, often aimed at reducing costs for consumers or encouraging the use of renewable energy sources.
Resource Title: Tracking SDG7 with the Multi-Tier Framework measuring Energy Access
Resource Description: The policy brief introduces the Multi-Tier Framework  as a tool to better track progress toward SDG 7.1 by measuring energy access across multiple dimensions—beyond binary metrics. It informs regulatory frameworks by offering granular data on reliability, affordability, and quality, helping policymakers design more targeted, inclusive, and effective energy access regulations and investments.

Concept Definition: Fossil fuel subsidies are financial support and incentives provided by governments to the fossil fuel industry, which can include tax breaks, grants, and price controls, aimed at reducing the cost of fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas.
Resource Title: Regulatory indicators for Sustainable Energy: A Global Scorecard for Policy Makers
Resource Description: This report presents a global scorecard assessing how conducive national policies and regulations are to advancing energy access, energy efficiency, and renewable energy. It highlights gaps and best practices, enabling governments to design better laws, targets, and incentives that drive inclusive, sustainable energy access.

Resource Title: Designing Responsible End-User Subsidies for Energy Access : A Toolkit Featuring Case Studies for the Design of Subsidies in Off-Grid Solar and Clean Cooking
Resource Description: This report is a practical toolkit for designing responsible end-user subsidies to expand access to off-grid solar and clean cooking. Drawing on experiences from ten countries, it offers guidance on targeting, delivery, and monitoring of subsidies to balance affordability, market impact, and scalability, supporting effective and context-sensitive energy access policies.

Lesson Title: Collaborative Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships
Description: This lesson explores the importance of multi-stakeholder partnerships and the role of international organizations, NGOs, development agencies, the private sector and local communities in advancing energy access objectives, as well as the associated challenges and conflicts.
Concept Definition: Community empowerment is the process of enabling individuals and groups within a community to gain control over their lives, make decisions, and take action to improve their social, economic, and environmental conditions.
Resource Title: Unlocking Smart Grid Opportunities in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies, 2023
Resource Description: This report provides guidance for policymakers on accelerating investment in smart and resilient electricity grids, particularly in emerging and developing economies where electricity demand is rising. It highlights the role of digital technologies in integrating renewable energy, enhancing grid efficiency, and unlocking data-driven system management, while offering practical policy recommendations and case studies to support implementation.

Concept Definition: A multi-stakeholder partnership is a collaborative arrangement involving various parties, such as governments, businesses, non-profits, and communities, working together to achieve common goals, often related to sustainable development or social impact.
Resource Title: Assessment of Energy Sources Using GIS
Resource Description: This report serves as a guide to applying Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for analyzing energy supply and demand at both global and local levels. It brings together cutting-edge research and methods for spatial and temporal analysis of energy systems, including fossil fuel mapping, renewable energy optimization, efficient deployment of power sources, and evaluation of their environmental impacts.

Key Concept: participatory diagnosis, design, monitoring, and evaluation
Concept Definition: A collaborative approach that involves stakeholders in the processes of diagnosing issues, designing solutions, monitoring progress, and evaluating outcomes to ensure that their perspectives and needs are integrated.
Resource Title: Digitalisation and Energy
Resource Description: This report  explores how digital technologies are reshaping energy systems by improving efficiency, sustainability, and connectivity across supply and demand sectors. It also highlights the challenges of digitalisation and offers guidance for policymakers  and industry leaders to harness its potential while managing emerging risks.

Lesson Title: The Energy Transition In Context
Chapter Title: Introduction to the Energy Transition Landscape
Description: This lesson will explore how a just transition is about more than just technical solutions or policy frameworks; it is about addressing deep-rooted socio-economic disparities, fostering participatory governance, and empowering all stakeholders to engage in the transition process.
Concept Definition: The energy transition refers to the global shift from fossil fuel-based energy systems to renewable and sustainable energy sources, aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and combating climate change.
Resource Title: World Energy Outlook 2024
Resource Description: This IEA’s report identifies and explores the biggest trends in energy demand and supply,  as well as what they mean for energy security, emissions and economic  development.

Concept Definition: Net zero refers to the balance between the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced and the amount removed from the atmosphere, resulting in no net increase in emissions.
Resource Title: Mapping Justice in National Climate Action: A Global Overview of Just Transition Policies
Resource Description: This report is an initial exploratory study of global trends in just transition policies and laws. It empirically reviews 159 policies and laws across 61 countries and the European Union that are available from the Climate Change Laws of the World database, and seeks to map which countries are integrating ideas associated with the just transition into domestic climate policy, and how.

Concept Definition: Carbon neutrality is the state of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by balancing the amount of carbon released with an equivalent amount of carbon offset or removed from the atmosphere.
Resource Title: World Energy Transitions Outlook 2024
Resource Description: IRENA’s 1.5°C Scenario, set out in the World Energy Transitions Outlook, presents a pathway to achieve the 1.5°C target by 2050, positioning electrification and efficiency as key transition drivers, enabled by renewable energy, clean hydrogen and sustainable biomass.

Lesson Title: Unpacking The Concept Of A Just Energy Transition
Description: This lesson outlines the just energy transition, focusing on fairness, equity, and inclusivity in sustainable energy shifts. Originating from labor rights, it addresses historical inequities through environmental, climate, and energy justice. Resource Description: This report underscores the critical role of local actors in advancing the global energy transition. The report advocates for inclusive, bottom-up approaches to complement national policies, emphasizing that empowering local stakeholders is essential for achieving climate goals and sustainable development.

Resource Description: The document emphasizes the role of integrated policies in advancing both climate action and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including SDG 7. The report includes eight building blocks, country case studies, and practical recommendations to help governments align policies across sectors for sustainable outcomes.

Resource Title: Connections between the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda; The case for policy coherence

It highlights both synergies and gaps, advocating for integrated policy approaches to enhance coherence between the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Resource Title: Driving Policy Coherence for Sustainable Development; ACCELERATING PROGRESS ON THE SDGS
Resource Description: This paper outlines strategies to enhance policy coherence for sustainable development in the context of complex, interconnected global challenges. The report also emphasizes institutional coordination, stakeholder engagement, and data-driven decision-making for more effective implementation.

Lesson Title: Strategic Foresight for Energy Governance

It includes scenario planning, stress-testing strategies, and actionable guidance to build resilient, future-ready public policies aligned with the 2030–2050 horizon.

Resource Description: This publication advocates for the use of strategic foresight in developing countries to enhance long-term planning and governance. The document encourages participatory approaches and regional collaboration to build foresight capacity and promote resilient development strategies

The report emphasizes the need for timely policy adjustments to accommodate changing costs, increasing deployment, and the integration of variable renewable energy sources.

Resource Description: This report examines the evolving landscape of clean energy technologies, focusing on manufacturing, trade, and supply chains. It analyzes six key technologies, solar PV, wind turbines, electric vehicles, batteries, electrolysers, and heat pumps, projecting their global market value to rise from $700 billion in 2023 to over $2 trillion by 2035. The report emphasizes the need for secure, resilient supply chains and coordinated industrial strategies to support the clean energy transition

Resource Title: Powering the Future Risk Governance for a Sustainable, Resilient and Inclusive Energy System
Resource Description: This UNDP policy brief advocates for integrating risk governance into energy planning to ensure sustainable, resilient, and inclusive energy systems. It explores how governments structure coordination between energy and climate policies, utilize long-term forecasting, and implement energy security strategies. The report offers insights into institutional design and policy integration to support more effective and resilient energy governance.

It highlights challenges such as coal dependence, investment readiness, and geopolitical shifts, including the U.S. withdrawal from climate finance commitments. Despite these hurdles, the commentary notes ongoing efforts by other nations to uphold JETP commitments and offers policy recommendations to enhance the effectiveness of these partnerships.

Lesson Title: Civic Engagements And Its Role in Energy Governance

Resource Description: This note explores the role of civic engagement and social accountability in strengthening governance. It argues that dynamic civil society involvement enhances both the effectiveness and legitimacy of public institutions. Highlighting vertical accountability mechanisms, such as citizen report cards and participatory budgeting—the document shows how collaboration between state and society can improve service delivery and democratic governance.

It emphasizes diversity, power dynamics, and trust-building while encouraging radical hospitality, adaptability, and respect for dissent. Resource Description: This guide examines gender equality in the sustainable energy transition.
